messages:
alex: Quick follow-up on the autoscaler RFC — ran into an edge case on dedicated GPU pools. Small bursty tenants are triggering repeated preemptions and then immediate reclaims, causing oscillation. Anyone seen this pattern or have an opinion on whether to adjust headroom calc vs admission window?

maya: yep seen it in staging. I think part of it is how we treat 'soft reservations' — we immediately free nodes on low-util and then predictive signals try to refill. Could we add a short cooldown after scale-down? :thinking_face: 

chris: +1 on cooldown. Also we should distinguish burst credits from steady quota in the admission policy. Right now those buckets are conflated so the allocator thinks tenant has no capacity when they actually have transient credits.

alex: that makes sense. Do we want cooldown to be operator-side (controller timers) or part of the autoscaler decision surface (admit/evict logic)?

dana: prefer operator-side for separation of concerns. Operator can enforce a `scale_down_delay` window so the autoscaler doesn't see ephemeral free capacity. Operator contract: it will not mark capacity as "available for immediate admit" until delay passed. This keeps admission deterministic.

maya: operator-side helps but we still need the autoscaler to respect burst-credit accounting or we'll under-provision. Proposal: keep operator cooldown + autoscaler aware of `burst_bucket` that decays over time.

chris: here's a tiny policy sketch — probably needs bikeshedding but illustrates fields we need:
```yaml
autoscaler:
  headroom_percent: 12  # baseline headroom to satisfy latency SLOs
  admission_window_sec: 15 # how long a newly freed slot is considered volatile
  scale_down_delay_sec: 180 # operator-side cooldown before exposing freed nodes
  burst_bucket_size: 30 # tokens per tenant for transient bursts
  burst_refill_rate_per_min: 5
```

sam: want to call out preemption jitter too. If eviction decision is immediate when a slot is needed, a tenant with small bursts will be evicted repeatedly. We should add a min-eviction-tenure (e.g., 60s) and prefer draining best-effort rather than instant kill. Also ensure tracing tags so we can link evict/reclaim cycles in telemetry.

alex: good call. Observability-wise we need an "eviction-cycle" metric and a preempt_count per-tenant so we can alert on >N evicts/min.

maya: test plan idea: synthetic load generator that produces short spikes (10s-30s) across N tenants while autoscaler is set to aggressive scale-down. Run w/ and w/o cooldown + burst buckets to measure oscillation.

dana: ops note: if we make operator-side changes, ensure API backward compatibility. New flags should default to current behavior (no cooldown) and opt-in via cluster config. Also add feature-gate for rollout.

alex: action items: (1) chris to draft a concrete autoscaler config PR with the fields above, (2) maya to build the spike test harness and run experiments, (3) dana to draft operator cooldown implementation + feature-gate, (4) sam to add telemetry hooks for eviction-cycle and preempt_count. I'll coordinate landing order so we don't flip default behavior.

infra-bot: scheduled: autoscaler-experiment-cluster for maya is provisioned (cluster id: aws-us-east-2-exp-42).

chris: I'll open the config PR today; will include example rollout plan and runbook for oscillation regression.

alex: thanks all — let's sync on results next Thurs. If anyone spots a simple tweak we can roll as hotfix, ping here. :thumbsup:
